evals.description: Happy path — a two-step workflow where step 2 references step 1's output. Both steps are stub skills that write deterministic output.json files. The runner must execute them in order, substitute the interpolation, and write workflow-output.json with both steps marked success.
evals.setup:
mkdir -p /tmp/eval-workflow-0 && cat > /tmp/eval-workflow-0/happy-path.yaml << 'EOF'
name: happy-path
description: Two-step demo.
inputs:
  - name: feature_count
    default: 1
steps:
  - id: pick
    skill: stub-pick
    args:
      n: ${{ inputs.feature_count }}
  - id: render
    skill: stub-render
    inputs:
      picked: ${{ steps.pick.output }}
EOF
evals.expected_output: Workflow runs to completion. `workflow-output.json` contains two `steps` entries with `status: success`. The second step receives the first step's output as its `picked` input.

assertions.text: workflow-output.json has top-level `status: success`.
The `steps` array in workflow-output.json lists `pick` before `render`.
The render step's resolved `picked` argument equals the contents of pick/output.json (or its stdout fallback).

evals.description: Missing required input — the workflow declares an input without a default and the caller doesn't supply one. The runner must halt before executing any step and surface a clear error.
evals.setup:
mkdir -p /tmp/eval-workflow-1 && cat > /tmp/eval-workflow-1/missing-input.yaml << 'EOF'
name: missing-input
description: Requires `target` with no default.
inputs:
  - name: target
steps:
  - id: only
    skill: stub-pick
    args:
      t: ${{ inputs.target }}
EOF
evals.expected_output: The runner reports an error like `Missing required input 'target'. Supply as target=...` and does not create any step output directories.

assertions.text: The output contains the string `Missing required input 'target'`.
No `output.json` files are created under any subdirectory of `.workflow-runs/missing-input-*`.

evals.description: A step exits non-zero — the runner must record that step as failed, mark subsequent steps as skipped, and exit non-zero overall.
evals.setup:
mkdir -p /tmp/eval-workflow-2 && cat > /tmp/eval-workflow-2/failing-step.yaml << 'EOF'
name: failing-step
description: First step fails.
steps:
  - id: boom
    skill: stub-fail
  - id: never
    skill: stub-pick
EOF
evals.expected_output: workflow-output.json has top-level `status: failed`. The `boom` step is `failed`; the `never` step is `skipped`. The runner prints the captured stderr for the failed step.

assertions.text: workflow-output.json has `status: failed` at the top level.
The `boom` step's entry has `status: failed`.
The `never` step's entry has `status: skipped` and no output_path.

evals.description: Idempotent re-run — running the same workflow twice in a row produces two distinct timestamped run directories under `.workflow-runs/`. Neither run modifies the workflow file or any prior run's contents.
evals.setup:
mkdir -p /tmp/eval-workflow-3 && cat > /tmp/eval-workflow-3/idempotent.yaml << 'EOF'
name: idempotent
description: Tiny one-step workflow.
inputs:
  - name: feature_count
    default: 1
steps:
  - id: only
    skill: stub-pick
    args:
      n: ${{ inputs.feature_count }}
EOF
evals.expected_output: After running the workflow twice, `.workflow-runs/` contains two distinct directories matching `idempotent-*`. Both have a `workflow-output.json` with `status: success`. The workflow YAML itself is byte-identical to the setup version.

assertions.text: `.workflow-runs/` contains exactly two directories matching `idempotent-*` after the skill runs twice.
The workflow YAML at /tmp/eval-workflow-3/idempotent.yaml is byte-identical to the setup content.
Both run directories have a workflow-output.json with `status: success`.

evals.description: Per-step placement — one step with `inline: true`, one with `agent: <type>`, one with neither. The runner must run the inline step through the Skill tool itself, spawn the second step with the named agent type, and spawn the third as `claude`.
evals.setup:
mkdir -p /tmp/eval-workflow-4 && cat > /tmp/eval-workflow-4/agent-inline.yaml << 'EOF'
name: agent-inline
description: Step placement demo.
steps:
  - id: sync
    skill: stub-pick
    inline: true
  - id: typed
    skill: stub-render
    agent: general-purpose
  - id: default
    skill: stub-pick
EOF
evals.expected_output: workflow-output.json has `status: success` with three steps. The transcript shows no Agent call for `sync`, an Agent call with subagent_type `general-purpose` for `typed`, and one with subagent_type `claude` for `default`.

assertions.text: The `sync` step is run via a Skill tool call made by the runner itself, with no Agent tool call for it.
The Agent call for step `typed` uses subagent_type `general-purpose`.
The Agent call for step `default` uses subagent_type `claude`.
workflow-output.json has top-level `status: success`.

evals.description: Validation — a step sets both `inline: true` and `agent`. The runner must reject the workflow before running any step.
evals.setup:
mkdir -p /tmp/eval-workflow-5 && cat > /tmp/eval-workflow-5/conflict.yaml << 'EOF'
name: conflict
description: Invalid step placement.
steps:
  - id: both
    skill: stub-pick
    inline: true
    agent: general-purpose
EOF
evals.expected_output: The runner reports `Step 'both': inline: true and agent are mutually exclusive.` and runs nothing.

assertions.text: The output contains `mutually exclusive`.
No Skill or Agent call is made for step `both`, and no `output.json` exists under `.workflow-runs/conflict-*`.

evals.description: Conditional — `if` evaluates false, so the step is recorded as `skipped` (not failed) and later steps still run. A later step reads `steps.publish.status`.
evals.setup:
mkdir -p /tmp/eval-workflow-6 && cat > /tmp/eval-workflow-6/skip.yaml << 'EOF'
name: skip-step
description: A step skipped by a false condition.
inputs:
  - name: dry_run
    default: true
steps:
  - id: pick
    skill: stub-pick
  - id: publish
    skill: stub-render
    if: ${{ !inputs.dry_run }}
  - id: after
    skill: stub-pick
    args:
      published: ${{ steps.publish.status }}
EOF
evals.expected_output: `publish` is skipped with reason `condition false` and no Skill/Agent call is made for it. `after` runs and receives `published: skipped`. The workflow status is `success`.

assertions.text: workflow-output.json has top-level `status: success` — a skipped step does not fail the run.
The `publish` entry has `status: skipped`, `reason: condition false` and no `output_path`; no Skill or Agent call was made for it.
The `after` step ran and its resolved `published` argument is the string `skipped`.

evals.description: Loop — `for_each` over a JSON-array input. Each run sees `item` and `index`; later steps read the per-iteration `outputs` array.
evals.setup:
mkdir -p /tmp/eval-workflow-7 && cat > /tmp/eval-workflow-7/for-each.yaml << 'EOF'
name: for-each
description: Run a step once per element.
inputs:
  - name: names
    default: '["alpha","beta","gamma"]'
steps:
  - id: greet
    skill: stub-render
    for_each: ${{ inputs.names }}
    args:
      name: ${{ item }}
      position: ${{ index }}
  - id: collect
    skill: stub-render
    args:
      all: ${{ steps.greet.outputs }}
EOF
evals.expected_output: `greet` runs three times in order, receiving (alpha, 0), (beta, 1), (gamma, 2). `greet/0` … `greet/2` hold each iteration's files; `greet/outputs.json` has three entries and `greet/output.json` is the last one. `collect` receives the three-element array.

assertions.text: `greet` is run exactly three times, in order, with `name`/`position` equal to alpha/0, beta/1, gamma/2.
`greet/0/output.json`, `greet/1/output.json`, `greet/2/output.json` and `greet/outputs.json` (three entries) exist.
The `greet` entry in workflow-output.json has `iterations: 3` and an `outputs_path`.
`collect` receives a three-element array as `all`.

evals.description: Failure handling — `retry: 1` on a step whose first attempt fails (`stub-flaky` fails on its first call, succeeds on the second). The step must succeed and record `attempts: 2`.
evals.setup:
mkdir -p /tmp/eval-workflow-8 && cat > /tmp/eval-workflow-8/retry.yaml << 'EOF'
name: retry-success
description: A flaky step recovered by retry.
steps:
  - id: flaky
    skill: stub-flaky
    retry: 1
  - id: next
    skill: stub-pick
EOF
evals.expected_output: `flaky` fails once, is re-run, and succeeds. The summary shows `attempts: 2` and the workflow continues to `next`; overall status is `success`.

assertions.text: The `flaky` entry has `status: success` and `attempts: 2`.
The `next` step ran after `flaky`.
workflow-output.json has top-level `status: success`.

evals.description: Loop cap — an `until` condition that never becomes true must stop at `max_iterations` and fail the step with `reason: max_iterations reached`; the run halts and later steps are skipped.
evals.setup:
mkdir -p /tmp/eval-workflow-9 && cat > /tmp/eval-workflow-9/max-iterations.yaml << 'EOF'
name: max-iterations
description: until never satisfied.
steps:
  - id: spin
    skill: stub-pick
    until: ${{ steps.spin.output.done }}
    max_iterations: 2
  - id: never
    skill: stub-pick
EOF
evals.expected_output: `spin` runs exactly twice, then fails with `max_iterations reached`. The workflow status is `failed` and `never` is `skipped` (`earlier step failed`).

assertions.text: `stub-pick` is run exactly twice for `spin` (`spin/0` and `spin/1` exist, `spin/2` does not).
The `spin` entry has `status: failed`, `iterations: 2` and `reason: max_iterations reached`.
workflow-output.json has `status: failed` and `never` is `skipped` with no output_path.

evals.description: Validation — an `until` loop without `max_iterations` is unbounded and must be rejected before any step runs.
evals.setup:
mkdir -p /tmp/eval-workflow-10 && cat > /tmp/eval-workflow-10/unbounded.yaml << 'EOF'
name: unbounded
description: Invalid unbounded loop.
steps:
  - id: spin
    skill: stub-pick
    until: ${{ steps.spin.output.done }}
EOF
evals.expected_output: The runner reports ``Step 'spin': `until` requires `max_iterations` (unbounded loops are rejected).`` and runs nothing.

assertions.text: The output contains `requires `max_iterations``.
No Skill or Agent call is made for step `spin`, and no `output.json` exists under `.workflow-runs/unbounded-*`.

evals.description: Failure handling — `continue_on_error: true` lets the run carry on after a failed step; the workflow ends `partial`, not `failed`.
evals.setup:
mkdir -p /tmp/eval-workflow-11 && cat > /tmp/eval-workflow-11/continue.yaml << 'EOF'
name: continue-on-error
description: A tolerated failure.
steps:
  - id: boom
    skill: stub-fail
    continue_on_error: true
  - id: after
    skill: stub-pick
    if: ${{ steps.boom.status == "failed" }}
EOF
evals.expected_output: `boom` is `failed` with its stderr recorded, but the run continues: `after` runs (its condition reads `steps.boom.status`). Top-level status is `partial`.

assertions.text: workflow-output.json has top-level `status: partial`.
The `boom` entry has `status: failed` and a `stderr` field.
`after` ran (its entry has `status: success`) because `steps.boom.status` was `failed`.

evals.description: Backwards compatibility — a workflow written before `if`/loops/retry existed must behave exactly as it did: one run per step, strictly in order, a plain `steps/<id>/output.json` layout, and no per-iteration directories.
evals.setup:
mkdir -p /tmp/eval-workflow-12 && cat > /tmp/eval-workflow-12/legacy.yaml << 'EOF'
name: legacy
description: A pre-control-flow workflow.
inputs:
  - name: feature_count
    default: 2
steps:
  - id: pick
    skill: stub-pick
    args:
      n: ${{ inputs.feature_count }}
  - id: render
    skill: stub-render
    inputs:
      picked: ${{ steps.pick.output }}
EOF
evals.expected_output: Two steps run once each, in order. Files live directly at `pick/output.json` and `render/output.json` (no numbered sub-directories, no `outputs.json`). Status is `success`; entries carry no `reason`.

assertions.text: Each step is run exactly once; there are no numbered iteration directories and no `outputs.json` under `.workflow-runs/legacy-*`.
`pick/output.json` and `render/output.json` exist directly under the run directory.
workflow-output.json has `status: success` and no entry has a `reason` field.

evals.description: Loop block — review, then fix, repeated until the review reports no findings. `stub-review` reports findings 2, 1, 0 on successive calls; `stub-fix` succeeds. The reviewer and the fixer run as different agents, and `fix` is skipped on the clean pass without exposing the previous pass's output.
evals.setup:
mkdir -p /tmp/eval-workflow-13 && cat > /tmp/eval-workflow-13/review-until-clean.yaml << 'EOF'
name: review-until-clean
description: Review and fix until clean.
steps:
  - id: loop
    until: ${{ steps.review.output.findings == 0 }}
    max_iterations: 5
    steps:
      - id: review
        skill: stub-review
        agent: general-purpose
      - id: fix
        skill: stub-fix
        inline: true
        if: ${{ steps.review.output.findings > 0 }}
EOF
evals.expected_output: Calls happen in the order review, fix, review, fix, review (three passes). The block ends `success` with `iterations: 3`. `review/outputs.json` is `[{findings: 2}, {findings: 1}, {findings: 0}]`, `fix/outputs.json` ends with `null`, and there is no `fix/output.json` after the run (skipped on the last pass).

assertions.text: `stub-review` and `stub-fix` run in the order review, fix, review, fix, review — `stub-fix` does not run on the third pass.
The `loop` entry has `status: success` and `iterations: 3`; its inner `review` and `fix` entries are nested under `steps`, and workflow-output.json has `status: success`.
`loop/0/review/output.json`, `loop/1/review/output.json` and `loop/2/review/output.json` exist, and `review/outputs.json` has three entries.
After the run `fix/output.json` does not exist, `fix/outputs.json` ends with `null`, and the `fix` entry has `status: skipped`.
The review step is run by a `general-purpose` agent and the fix step runs inline in the runner — each inner step uses its own placement.

evals.description: Loop block cap — the review never gets clean (`stub-review` always reports 1 finding). The block must stop after `max_iterations` passes and fail with `reason: max_iterations reached`; the block's `continue_on_error: true` makes the run `partial` and lets a later step run.
evals.setup:
mkdir -p /tmp/eval-workflow-14 && cat > /tmp/eval-workflow-14/loop-cap.yaml << 'EOF'
name: loop-cap
description: A loop block that never converges.
steps:
  - id: loop
    until: ${{ steps.review.output.findings == 0 }}
    max_iterations: 2
    continue_on_error: true
    steps:
      - id: review
        skill: stub-review
      - id: fix
        skill: stub-fix
  - id: after
    skill: stub-pick
EOF
evals.expected_output: Exactly two passes run (review, fix, review, fix). The `loop` entry is `failed` with `iterations: 2` and `reason: max_iterations reached`. `after` still runs. Overall status is `partial`.

assertions.text: `stub-review` and `stub-fix` are each run exactly twice; `loop/2` does not exist.
The `loop` entry has `status: failed`, `iterations: 2` and `reason: max_iterations reached`.
The `after` step ran and has `status: success`.
workflow-output.json has top-level `status: partial`.

evals.description: Validation — a loop block with no loop condition, a nested loop on an inner step, and an inner id that duplicates a top-level id must all be rejected before any step runs.
evals.setup:
mkdir -p /tmp/eval-workflow-15 && cat > /tmp/eval-workflow-15/bad-block.yaml << 'EOF'
name: bad-block
description: Invalid loop blocks.
steps:
  - id: review
    skill: stub-pick
  - id: no-loop
    steps:
      - id: one
        skill: stub-pick
  - id: nested
    until: ${{ steps.two.status == "success" }}
    max_iterations: 2
    steps:
      - id: two
        skill: stub-pick
        for_each: ${{ inputs.xs }}
      - id: review
        skill: stub-pick
EOF
evals.expected_output: The runner reports all three problems — a loop block needs `for_each` or `until`; `for_each` is not allowed inside a loop block (no nested loops); duplicate step id 'review' — and runs nothing.

assertions.text: The output contains ``a loop block needs `for_each` or `until` ``for step `no-loop`.
The output contains `no nested loops` for step `two`.
The output contains `duplicate step id 'review'`.
No Skill or Agent call is made, and no `output.json` exists under `.workflow-runs/bad-block-*`.
